title: Lingering object references for export vars in editor
body:
### Tested versions

Tested heavily on v4.5.beta7.mono.official [4ebf67c12]
Additional lingering references in v4.6.2.rc1.mono.official [257ac3532]

### System information

Godot v4.5.beta7.mono - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6094) - AMD Ryzen 7 1700 Eight-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.95 GiB memory

### Issue description

I am working with tool scripts, fully in the editor, and track the lifetime of my resources via holding WeakRef of them.
Export variables holding resources will sometimes create strong references to objects beyond what undoredo history or current inspector context requires.

#### Briefly the findings:
- In 4.5 when deleting an object from an export var in the editor, if it was unfolded (its editable content exposed), the editor will hold onto a strong reference to the object even after you clear the export var and throw that object away.
- In 4.6 this unfolded strong reference is still there. In addition, 4.6 holds onto a strong reference for every object regardless. I have not tested extensively in 4.6, and don't have any suggestions for what might be holding this.

#### Why do I think this is important?
- Mostly because I think it is completely unnecessary for the Godot editor to be holding onto references of objects that we have thrown away. When the undoredo history is gone, there is absolutely no reason the editor should have those references.
- Garbage collection or some kind of background process can eventually come and clear these references. If your object has some cleanup on predelete, this will now happen in a thread where many things are not allowed. This can then throw errors on things that are not allowed at that time. It seems to me that it is unreasonable that cleanup on NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE should be coded differently than is required in a live setting, just because the editor is not so mindful about what it is holding strong and weak references of, and when it deems it appropriate to clean up after itself.
- Personally, I think that it should be considered a bug to hold onto a strong reference to a developer generated object, if the developer has no way of accessing that object anymore, and no undo can retrieve it anymore. But that is my personal opinion.

### Steps to reproduce

Briefly:
- Have an export var in a scene with a tool script.
- Assign an object to that export var.
- Track a WeakRef of the object.
- Delete the object.
- Clear undoredo history.
- Clear inspector context.
- Get reference of WeakRef and read how many references are still being held.

For more in-depth, I would recommend checking either of my repro projects. They are basically the same, just one written in 4.5 and the other in 4.6. (slight different syntax, and some different results)

The projects come with a plugin with a button that will flush all undoredo history, as well as clear the context of the current edited object. (You may look at the code to see if you agree this is what the code is doing)

Reproduction to observe the issue in the projects:
- Open Main.tscn
- Create a Resource in the reference_checker export var
- Unfold the Resource (click on it)
- Clear the export var
- Flush undoredo history
- PrintRefs (export_tool_button in main.gd)
- Observe any Resource that was unfolded when they were deleted have one more strong refcount than those that were folded when they were cleared. (It will say the refcount is 2. 1 for the reference we are holding to print out the reference, and 1 from the Godot editor) (In 4.6 it will say 3. 1 for your reference, 1 for the unfolded reference, and 1 unknown)

[memory-leak-4.5.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26399437/memory-leak-4.5.zip)
[memory-leak-4.6.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26399441/memory-leak-4.6.zip)
